body.text: If someone curses you, plug your ears; if someone shows you a look of disgust, cover your eyes. It is the almighty god who came out of the dream, it is the EGO that is forever stable. Stay here forever, because you can no longer hear the cursing; why not stay here forever? You can't see the road out anyway.
Relax, I'll make the decisions for you. You just can't escape anymore, that's all.
Perception is the flesh; cognition is the soul. Dissociation is making the soul unable to hear the flesh.

The NMDA receptor was originally a ferry crossing, carrying 'what is felt' over to 'what is thought'. After antagonism, the ferry stops running: you see the cake, but you can't cognize it as interesting; you smell mint and lemon, but can't judge it as worthwhile. The world is still there, but it no longer holds for you. The dissociated person's world is truly boring — not blind, but the chain from 'exists' to 'what it's like' to 'what should be done' has been dismantled link by link.

Consider two people walking into the same shop. A sees a cylinder, a black glaze, a few red fruits, thinks only that it's big, and turns to leave. B sees chocolate, hazelnut, nuts, strawberry, sees the glitter on the side, smells mint and lemon, and thinks: this is so novel, I should be a little good to myself. The cake is the same cake; what separates A and B is that dismantled chain.

At a low level, you operate yourself like actions that don't need thinking about; at a medium level, like pulling strings on a puppet, very unreal; at a high level, you can't perceive that you're operating yourself at all. You observe yourself like observing another person, like controlling a game character. The body isn't yours, like arms gone numb from pressure. You ask 'who am I', ask 'what is the meaning of being alive', ask 'what is this world' — nobody answers, because answering also needs that dismantled chain. What people call an out-of-body experience is really the soul standing beside the body, unable to find the door back.

At the highest dissociation, emotion is cut off from body control entirely, like a dead sleep. Ego death often comes with a coma: as if you had already died. Dissociation is a process of approaching death.

But it gives you things too. Dissociate the past pain away, and what's left is only the joy of driving the invader out — euphoria, happiness. Pain is 'dissociated out' rather than 'suppressed'; that's dissociative anesthesia. Fatigue perception drops, so there's motor enhancement: you can jump and jump, run without feeling tired. Emotion is isolated from the outside world, protecting you from emotional harm and quietly taking your empathy with it. Disinhibition makes you dare to strike up conversations, to speak your mind, to think up odd but effective solutions — some mistake this for 'waking up'.

The price is in the dark. Memories become harder to recall: the bad ones don't come, but the good days don't either. Learning ability drops; getting familiar with a neighbourhood, learning a subject, both get harder. Depersonalization is seeded. And the most insidious thing is the rewriting of cognition: dissociation first empties out your sense of 'harm', then lets the behaviour you did while dissociated be relearned and integrated back — so 'swallowing a lot of pills is unreasonable' becomes 'swallowing a lot of pills is reasonable', and 'incontinence matters' becomes 'incontinence doesn't matter'. You think there's no problem because your cognition has already been reshaped. Try judging your present self by the morality you used to have.
